reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives define a triadic structure of quarterback performance: drop rate measures receiver coordination, pressure index quantifies external stress, and bad throw ratio evaluates internal execution. These combine into a strategic tensor where each component reflects distinct failure modes—reliability, resilience, and precision. The dual nature emerges in that high drop rates correlate with low pressure indices, suggesting defensive coordination rather than individual failure. Conversely, high bad throw ratios often accompany elevated pressure indices, indicating cognitive load effects. This duality implies that optimal performance requires balancing receiver support with quarterback composure. Failure modes include: 1) Over-reliance on receivers (high drop rate), 2) Overexertion under pressure (high pressure index), 3) Inconsistent execution (high bad throw ratio). Each mode can be modeled as a stochastic process governed by team-level variables such as offensive line quality and defensive scheme complexity.
